title: The innkeeper (1203)
hook: Dominic stays up all night talking with an innkeeper who held other beliefs

segments.voice: Yesterday, a Franciscan day at home, and the end of three weeks with Francis. Your line was praise and simplicity. What did you let go, and what did you praise? Day one thousand two hundred twenty-nine.

An inn in the city of Toulouse, in the south of France. It's late. Two travelers from Spain have come in off the road: a bishop named Diego, on an errand for his king, and a priest of his cathedral, a Castilian named Dominic. They're tired. They want a bed. But Dominic gets talking with the man who runs the inn, and he discovers that his host holds beliefs very different from his own. He could nod politely and go upstairs. Dominic doesn't go upstairs. Today, the conversation that, by tradition, started an order.
screen: `AN INN IN TOULOUSE, LATE.` → `TWO TRAVELERS FROM SPAIN.` → `DOMINIC DOESN'T GO UPSTAIRS.`

segments.voice: The story is told by Jordan of Saxony, who followed Dominic as head of his order and wrote down how it began. The innkeeper, Jordan says, belonged to the movement the Church called heresy and historians call the Cathars. They taught that the material world was not the good work of a good God, and they lived lives of hard self-denial that impressed their neighbors. So Dominic, in Jordan's telling, spent the whole night with his host, talking earnestly and with warmth. Not shouting him down. Not threatening. Talking, and listening, and talking again, until dawn. And by morning, Jordan says, the man could not resist the wisdom and the spirit of what he heard, and he returned to the Catholic faith. Now notice what the story chooses to remember. Not a crowd. Not a church council. One man, one table, one long night. A line from the first letter of Peter fits the scene. In the Douay-Rheims it asks believers to be "ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you." And the verse after it says how: with modesty and fear. Tradition says that night in Toulouse planted something in Dominic. Before it, he was a canon of his cathedral, praying in its choir. After it, he wanted to spend his life doing exactly that: explaining, patiently, to people who saw the world another way. That's what the order he founded would be called: the Preachers.
screen: `JORDAN OF SAXONY TELLS IT.` · `A HOST WHO SAW THE WORLD ANOTHER WAY.` · `ONE TABLE, ONE NIGHT, UNTIL DAWN.` · `A LIFE OF PATIENT EXPLAINING.` · then, large: `READY ALWAYS TO SATISFY EVERY ONE THAT ASKETH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: get ready for a long, patient conversation. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind someone who sees the world very differently from you: about faith, or politics, or how to live. Picture sitting across a table from them late at night, with nowhere to be. What would you ask them, really wanting the answer? Choose one question. Then notice what you'd have to set down to hear the answer: the need to win, the clock, the speech you've already rehearsed. If you pray, you can pray for that person by name. The bell holds the time.
The innkeeper. The man who held other beliefs, and the night Dominic spent at his table, talking until dawn. Today's word.
Your line: all night talking. Today, ask your one question, and then stay in the conversation longer than feels comfortable, without trying to win it. Day one thousand two hundred twenty-nine.

howItsDone: Dominicans tell the story of the innkeeper as the seed of their order, and Dominican friars and sisters still give much of their lives to study, preaching and long conversations with people who hold other views.

notes: Claims rule: the title's date is not repeated in the voice.

Jordan's account paraphrased: Diego of Osma traveling on the king of Castile's business, with Dominic; their host in Toulouse a heretic; Dominic disputing with him through the night 'strenuously and fervently' until he brought him back to the faith. Confirm wording ('earnestly and with warmth'; 'could not resist the wisdom and the spirit').
Cathar belief summarized fairly and briefly: the material world not the work of the good God; lives of hard self-denial that impressed neighbors.
Dominic described as 'a priest of his cathedral' / 'a quiet canon' (canon regular, sub-prior of Osma). Confirm.
1 Peter 3:16 'with modesty and fear' is paraphrased; Douay-Rheims wording of 3:15 to confirm.
